name: Aldous Huxley
summary: Huxley, author of Brave New World, was a critic of totalitarianism of left and right, of Big Business and Big Government, and of nationalism and war. He argued for decentralized, self-governing small groups, co-operative and mixed enterprises, wide distribution of property, non-violence and disarmament, and for population limitation. He saw technology, propaganda and over-organization as threats to freedom.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Ends and Means calls for disarmament, unilateral if necessary, as a condition of peace; it does not spell out complete abolition.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He says true aristocracy can exist only where there are no hereditary advantages other than talent (ss3 Political Democracy).

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: Ends and Means says machinery of arbitration such as the Hague Court should exist and be used instead of armed violence.

arms-reduction.rationale: Ends and Means names disarmament, unilateral if necessary, among the things that make for peace.

character-from-environment.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says heredity is no less significant than culture and rejects the view that people are products of their social environment alone.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: As a complete pacifist he condemns the methods of modern war, including its attacks on civilians (ss2 ch. IX).

collective-defense.rationale: Ends and Means says 'collective security' in practice means one system of military alliances opposed to another.

collective-farming.rationale: He cautions against rapid collectivization of agriculture and criticizes Soviet forced collectivization (ss2 ch. V).

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He criticizes colonies run for the profit of financiers and industrialists and proposes international mandate control (ss2 ch. IX).

conscription.rationale: Ends and Means lists conscription and militarized education among the evils of nationalism and dictatorship.

cooperative-communities.rationale: He favours small self-governing groups and co-operative enterprises, but does not call for common ownership of all property (ss2 chs. V, VIII).

decide-locally.rationale: Ends and Means states that the desirable context for reform is decentralization and self-government all round.

democracy-best.rationale: Brave New World Revisited holds that people given a fair chance can govern themselves better than authorities can govern them; Ends and Means says democratic freedom is good for those who enjoy it though it can disappoint.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says the right to vote by itself is no guarantee of liberty, and democracy in a large society is almost meaningless without autonomous groups of manageable size.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He says the dictatorship of the proletariat is in fact dictatorship by a small privileged minority and does not lead to liberty (ss2 ch. VII).

direct-votes.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says the right to vote alone is no guarantee of liberty and warns of dictatorship by referendum; Ends and Means says many are by nature unsuited to large-scale political questions.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Brave New World Revisited rejects the 'Social Ethic' that places the group above the individual.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Ends and Means says imbeciles rise by hereditary right and notes with approval that most modern societies abolished the hereditary principle in politics.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He opposes imperial autarky and lists abandonment of economic nationalism among the things that make for peace (ss2 ch. IX).

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Ends and Means rejects League of Nations military and economic sanctions as war under another name.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says each person is biologically unique, so freedom and tolerance are great goods and regimentation a misfortune.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Ends and Means criticizes collective security as rival military alliance blocs that lead to war.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Ends and Means says complete equality of income is probably impossible and perhaps undesirable, but that steps toward equalization ought to be taken and a maximum fixed.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: He says people can govern themselves 'given a fair chance', and that a people passing abruptly from despotism to self-rule cannot use it at once (ss1 ch. IV).

experts-over-public.rationale: Brave New World Revisited laments young people content to be ruled by an oligarchy of experts, while Ends and Means says big-city administration must be centrally planned by experts.

free-trade.rationale: He praises British free trade and calls for quotas to be abolished and tariffs lowered (ss2 ch. IX).

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Ends and Means says economic warfare through tariffs, quotas and currency devaluations leads sooner or later to military warfare, and that tariff barriers should be lowered.

future-generations.rationale: Brave New World Revisited urges a world-wide policy of conserving soil, forests and minerals and criticizes squandering the planet's resources.

gradual-change.rationale: Ends and Means says desirable changes should be made, wherever possible, by extending methods people already know and approve.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Brave New World Revisited calls preserving the unfit both obviously good (helping the unfortunate) and obviously bad (genetic contamination), an ethical dilemma needing a middle way.

history-own-civilization.rationale: He criticizes nationalistic history teaching as propaganda (ss2 ch. XII).

initiating-nondefensive-force-unjustifie.rationale: A complete pacifist, he rejects violence as a means of policy, including war, whoever starts it (ss2 chs. IV, IX).

keep-public-institutions-small.rationale: Ends and Means argues the units of self-government should be groups of optimum size (about ten to thirty); Brave New World Revisited says self-government is in inverse ratio to numbers.

leader-cult.rationale: Ends and Means says Duces and Fuehrers arise because people worship Caesars and Napoleons, and condemns the adored dictator-figures of Rome, Berlin and Moscow.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: He says there should be legislation limiting what candidates may spend on campaigns, and barring anti-rational propaganda (ss1 ch. XII).

limit-population.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says the birth rate must be reduced with all possible speed to the point where it does not exceed the death rate.

local-production.rationale: Ends and Means calls for decentralization of industry and its association with agriculture; Brave New World Revisited lists dispersal of production and village industry among schemes of men of good will.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says commercial mass communication feeds an infinite appetite for distractions, and that many will settle for bread and circuses and renounce freedom.

maximum-personal-income.rationale: Ends and Means says there should be no great difficulty in imposing an absolute maximum wage, and discusses what ratio to set.

means-match-ends.rationale: Ends and Means is built on the claim that desirable ends can be reached only by desirable means, and that undesirable means bring undesirable results.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: A complete pacifist, he rejects war as an instrument of policy (ss2 ch. IX).

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: He criticizes the 'fire-eaters' calling for military action against Fascist states, as it militarizes democracies (ss2 ch. VII).

military-superiority.rationale: Ends and Means condemns the arms race and rearmament and calls for disarmament, unilateral if necessary.

nation-first.rationale: He treats exclusive nationalism as idolatry and a cause of war (ss2 ch. IV).

natural-rulers.rationale: He proposes government by the 'naturally best' men of tested ability (ss3 Political Democracy) and a test of character for politicians (ss2 ch. XI).

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Ends and Means says small-scale industrial democracy is almost equally incompatible with capitalism (many petty dictators) and state socialism (one totalitarian dictatorship).

night-watchman-state.rationale: He proposes state-directed decentralization of industry, state supervision of public corporations and international planning, well beyond police protection (ss2 ch. V).

office-by-exam.rationale: Ends and Means notes that civil servants are appointed by examination and proposes applying tests of fitness and character to politicians too.

one-party-rule.rationale: Ends and Means condemns the single-party dictatorships of Russia, Germany and Italy, with their secret police, censorship and cult of the leader.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Ends and Means sets out how self-government can be applied to the daily lives of ordinary men and women, through work groups, co-operatives and local bodies.

party-controls-media.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says democracy depends on adequate information and that dictatorships survive by censoring and distorting facts.

patriotic-education.rationale: He condemns authoritarian, nationalistic state schooling and patriotic propaganda in history teaching (ss2 ch. XII).

person-over-state.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says societies are good only insofar as they help individuals realize their potentialities and lead a creative life, and condemns standardizing individuals.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Ends and Means says violence to impose reform is criminally rash because it produces only the effects of violence, and calls for methods of non-violence.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He says nations must sacrifice some sovereign rights for international planning (ss2 ch. IX).

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says rising numbers press on resources, leaving hundreds of millions undernourished and overcrowded.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: He describes the English press as in the hands of a few rich men who rule without responsibility (ss3), and in 1958 calls Western media control 'economic censorship' (ss1 ch. IV).

proportional-representation.rationale: He argues proportional representation makes parliaments instruments of anarchy and led Italy to fascism (ss3 Political Democracy).

public-ownership.rationale: Ends and Means backs extending public-utility corporations (Port of London Authority, BBC) with autonomous management, yet says state socialism breeds a centralized totalitarian dictatorship; he prefers co-operative and mixed concerns.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Ends and Means proposes extending limitation of profit and state supervision in the public interest, already applied to public-utility corporations, to wider fields.

restore-past-order.rationale: Brave New World Revisited calls romantic accounts of the Middle Ages misleading, citing the chronic frustration of its rigid hierarchy.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: He argues 'the more violence, the less revolution' and that a violent revolution can produce only the effects of violence, citing the Jacobin and Bolshevik dictatorships (ss2 ch. IV).

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says life in large cities is anonymous and bad for mental health and urges reviving the small country community.

sacred-nation.rationale: Ends and Means calls nationalism an idolatry, with the nation among the local divinities that self-transcendence leaves behind.

separated-powers.rationale: He calls legal checks and balances 'institutionalized mistrust', insufficient but 'a great deal better than nothing' (ss2 ch. VIII).

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Ends and Means proposes bringing change by developing existing institutions (co-operatives, public corporations, taxation).

space-expansion.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says a settlement on the moon would do nothing to make life tolerable for the earth's growing billions.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He accepts Marx's point that the state exists, among other reasons, to secure a ruling class its privileges, under feudalism, capitalism and state Socialism alike (ss2 ch. VII).

state-directs-investment.rationale: He proposes a public investment trust and state supervision of large-scale production (ss2 ch. V).

state-harmful.rationale: Ends and Means says the state is worthy of abolition insofar as it is a ruling-class tool, but that complex societies need a coordinating organization and he keeps the word 'state'.

strong-leader.rationale: Ends and Means says it is unsafe to concentrate power in a ruling oligarchy or a Fuehrer; Brave New World Revisited warns that concentrated power drives toward totalitarianism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says a dictatorship sustains itself by censoring and distorting facts, and Huxley defends freedom of thought and the right to dissent.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Ends and Means describes tariffs, quotas and competitive devaluations as economic warfare that leads to military warfare, and says tariff barriers should be lowered.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Ends and Means cites death duties as an accepted tool that can reduce economic inequality and shift control of large-scale production and finance from private hands.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Ends and Means says taxation and death duties can be used to reduce economic inequality between classes and that steps toward equalization ought to be taken.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says technological advance drives concentration of power, and Britannica notes Brave New World expresses Huxley's distrust of twentieth-century trends in technology.

total-state.rationale: Brave New World Revisited warns against the drift toward totalitarian control of everything and calls freedom supremely valuable.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Ends and Means puts Soviet Russia's army, secret police, censorship and adored dictator alongside Hitler's and Mussolini's, and condemns both.

uniformed-youth.rationale: He condemns regimenting children through military drill and the 'Prussian' school discipline of the dictatorships (ss2 chs. VII, XII).

war-builds-character.rationale: He opposes war and the militarism it breeds, which he says forms a tradition of violence (ss2 chs. IV, IX).

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Brave New World Revisited argues that power follows property and that means of production concentrated in Big Business and Big Government threaten democracy, so property must be distributed widely.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Brave New World Revisited says that if you believe in democracy you should arrange to distribute property as widely as possible, and praises the advocates of decentralised property.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ends and Means prefers co-operative (producer and consumer) and mixed concerns as forms of ultimate industrial control, as the ones compatible with self-government in industry.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Ends and Means endorses Dubreuil's scheme of self-governing work groups that elect leaders and share pay, saying it would introduce genuine democracy into the factory.

notes: Answers rest on his mature works (Ends and Means 1937, Brave New World Revisited 1958); Proper Studies (1927) is more elitist about democracy and heredity and is not used for answers. Themes searched: economy, government, liberty, world, ecology, society, means; everything not stated in the sources is null.
